title: Deactivating Net 30 keeps every customer on it, shown as inactive
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure COD is the shop's default for new customers.
  • Create customer A and vendor A for this test, both on Net 30.
  • Start on the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click the "⋯" at the right of the "Net 30" row.
  2. Click "Deactivate".
  3. Open customer A's customer page.
  4. Open Edit Customer.
  5. Open vendor A's vendor page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens.
  • "Deactivate" is available (not greyed) although Net 30 is in use.

Step 2:

  • The toast "Net 30 deactivated" shows.

Step 3:

  • The customer card's "Credit term" reads "Net 30 (Inactive)".

Step 4:

  • The Credit Terms dropdown shows "Net 30 (Inactive)" selected.

Step 5:

  • The vendor card's "Credit term" reads "Net 30 (Inactive)".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11671 (Story 2, Row menu actions)

  • S2-E3: “Deactivating a standard term in use (for example Net 30 with 290 customers) is allowed; those customers keep Net 30, shown "Net 30 (Inactive)" on their card and in Edit Customer.”
  • S2-R7: “"Deactivate" acts at once, without a confirmation: the term moves to the Inactive tab, both tab counts update, and a success toast shows "{name} deactivated". Every customer and vendor on the term keeps it (Story 5: New Customer and Edit Customer, Story 6: Vendors).”
  • S2-N5: “A term in use shows "Edit" and "Delete Credit Term" blocked with the "Used by ..." reason; "Deactivate" stays available.”
  • Key Decisions: “Deactivating a term hides it from the customer and vendor pickers only. Everyone on it keeps it, shown as "{name} (Inactive)" on their card and in Edit, until someone picks another term; invoices print the plain name; it can be reactivated at any time.”
  • Terminology: “Inactive → A deactivated term: absent from the customer and vendor pickers, still held by whoever had it, and shown as "{name} (Inactive)" on their card and in Edit.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
